test_title: PYST 30 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 24 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
**Change the following sentence into the Active form.**

It has been being debated for months whether the new enacted or not.

options.text: They have been debating for months whether the new law will be enacted or not.
The new law will be enacted or not, which they have been debating for months.
Whether the new law will be enacted or not has been debated for months.
They have been being debated for months whether the new law will be enacted or not.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tense Identification:** The original sentence "has been being debated" is in the **Present Perfect Continuous Passive** voice.
 
• **Active Voice Rule:** To convert Present Perfect Continuous Passive to Active, the structure changes from "has/have been being + V3" to "**has/have been + V1-ing**".
 
• **Subject Placement:** Since the passive sentence uses the dummy subject "It," we introduce a logical subject like "They" to perform the action in the active voice.
 
• **Completing the Context:** While the original prompt had a slight typo ("whether the new enacted or not"), Option 1 correctly restores the likely intended meaning by adding "law will be."
 
• **Verb Conversion:** "Has been being debated" becomes "have been debating" to match the plural subject "They."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"They have been debating for months whether the new law will be enacted or not."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** This is a complex sentence that rearranges the clauses but does not properly address the active transformation of the main verb.
 
• **Option 3:** This sentence is still in the **Passive Voice** ("has been debated"), just using the "whether" clause as the subject.
 
• **Option 4:** "Have been being debated" is still passive and grammatically redundant in this active context.
